subject: Observability & evals discovery — recap and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@finlytic.com>, David Huang <david.huang@finlytic.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability & evals discovery — recap and proposed next steps

Samantha / David — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed short plan so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Lack of reliable telemetry for model regressions (hard to tie quality drops to model, prompt, or infra changes).
- Unclear tracing from request -> model variant -> routing policy (makes incident RCA slow).
- Cost volatility / unexpected token spend on bursty workloads.

Current stack you described:
- In-house API gateway + SQS for async jobs
- Open-source models hosted on a mix of on-prem GPU and cloud spot instances
- Internal logging in ELK but no per-request prompt/response golden-set tracing

Success criteria we agreed on:
1) Observable regression detection: set up dashboards and alerts that signal model quality degradation vs. baseline prompts.
2) Request-level traceability: be able to trace an output back to the exact prompt, model variant, and routing decision.
3) Predictable token spend: confidence bands and a pre-flight cost estimation for POC traffic.

Immediate POC scope (proposed, 3 weeks):
- Instrumentation: add tracing hook in your gateway to include request metadata (prompt ID, session ID, model variant).
- Golden prompt set: define 50 prompts from your top intents for automated evals (we’ll provide templates).
- Dashboards: per-model latency/quality/cost dashboard plus a regression alert rule.
- Rollout guardrails: canary thresholds + automatic fallback to a cheaper variant when quality > X drop.

Attachments: I attached a one-pager on Redwood observability and a draft POC scope workbook (finlytic_poc_scope.xlsx) for your review.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the 50 golden prompts (we can take a first pass if you send samples).
2) We schedule a technical sync (30–45m) next week to go over tracing hook details (gateway headers, staging access).
3) We exchange a simple NDA/POC SOW — I’ll share a short SOW and timeline.

Would you be available for a tech sync on Tue/Wed next week (May 18/19)? If you prefer, I can send a calendar invite for Tue May 18 at 10am PT.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

Jordan — really helpful recap, thanks. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Priority order: 1) regression detection 2) tracing 3) cost visibility. Regression alerts that we can test against our monthly release cadence are most important.
- We can share an initial set of ~60 candidate prompts (mix of API and UI flows) by EOD Tue. Can you and Neha mark which fit the golden set best?
- Tech sync: Tue May 18 10am PT works for David and me. Please send the invite.

One question: on rollout guardrails — would the fallback be to a quantized variant or to a completely different family? Our infra team favors staying within the same family to reduce inference divergence.

Also, procurement heads up: we are targeting a July pilot start; procurement will need a concise SOW + standard security questionnaire.

Thanks — Samantha

Subject: Re: Observability & evals discovery — tracing hooks + data handling notes

Samantha — quick technical notes ahead of the sync: 

- Tracing hook: we typically ask for a short header bundle from the gateway (x-rl-session, x-rl-prompt-id, x-rl-user-id). We can provide a small middleware snippet (Node/Python) to emit these.
- Data residency / PII: if any prompts include PII, mark them and we’ll route those requests to a dedicated private pool (no shared logs). We will not persist raw prompt text in long-term logs unless you opt in for training or debug sessions — ephemeral traces are retained for 14 days by default.
- Golden set evals: we recommend a seed of 50, but accept your 60 and we’ll prune to the most representative 40–50. We run automated quality checks (exact-match, edit-distance, and human spot checks).

I’ll bring a short instrumentation checklist to the Tue call and we can agree on the headers and staging endpoints.

-Neha
